issue: Pragmatics: announcing 내릴 거예요 (detached future plan) to a taxi driver is not how you ask to stop — Koreans say 여기서 내릴게요 or 세워 주세요. -(으)ㄹ 거예요 reports a plan; -(으)ㄹ게요 commits an action for the listener's benefit, which is exactly what this functional travel phrase needs. As written, learners will deploy a line no driver hears from natives.

fix.grammar: 내릴게요 (naerilgeyo) — -(으)ㄹ게요 signals an action for the listener: 여기서 내릴게요 = I'll get off here.

내릴게요.en: I'll get off (informing/volunteering to the listener)

issue: Offer pragmatics: the tip itself glosses 제가 살 거예요 as 'my treat!', but when treating someone Koreans say 제가 살게요 / 제가 낼게요 — the -(으)ㄹ게요 offering form. Plain -(으)ㄹ 거예요 is a plan statement and sounds oddly flat in this bill-fight exchange; every textbook contrasts exactly these two endings here.

fix.grammar: 살게요 (salgeyo) — -(으)ㄹ게요 is the offering form: 제가 살게요 = my treat!

issue: Same -(으)ㄹ 거예요 / -(으)ㄹ게요 confusion as ko-0641: claiming the bill is a speaker-commitment offer, so natives say 제가 계산할게요. 제가 계산할 거예요 reads as reporting a decision to a third party rather than volunteering at the table.

fix.grammar: 계산할게요 (gyesanhalgeyo) — volunteer with -(으)ㄹ게요: 제가 계산할게요 = I've got this.

계산할게요.en: I'll pay, I'll get the bill (offering)

issue: Register mix: 와/과 is the written/formal comitative; this deck's canonical spoken 'with' is (이)랑 (친구랑 on ko-0666, ko-0789). 가족과 in a 해요체 diary sentence breaks the one-canonical-level rule — the same offender class already flagged on ko-0165 in the wave-1 audit.

fix.english: On Friday we ate out as a family.

issue: Word-order calque: sentence-initial bare 처음 ('처음 순두부찌개를 먹었어요') mirrors English 'For the first time, I ate...'. Natural Korean puts 처음 directly before the verb (순두부찌개를 처음 먹었어요) or uses 처음으로. Reorder only — no new vocabulary needed.

fix.english: I tried soft-tofu stew for the first time.
